description.p: A native Nostr client with a GPU-rendered UI and a local-first event store: a follows-driven timeline, threads, reactions, zaps, reposts, and direct messages, all served from an LMDB cache on your disk and kept fresh by one live subscription.

Inline video plays through GStreamer, click to play, one player at a time, no autoplay: a tile's preview is a poster the publisher attached, a blurhash, or a first frame decoded locally, the video itself never downloads before you tap, and strict Tor keeps even the preview off. Keys stay in your secret store, relays are yours to pick (NIP-65), and private preferences sync end-to-end encrypted through NIP-78.

The attachment-interop fix, hours after 0.7.0: a note's attached image or video now puts its URL in the event content beside the imeta tag. NIP-92 lets a client ignore an imeta that matches no content URL, and the strict ones did: the attachment showed in Satori and nowhere else. Comments get the same treatment, and an author who pastes the URL themselves gets no duplicate. Picture and video posts were already self-contained by design.

The interoperability release. Comments render and compose on articles (the reader grew a comments section with a reply affordance), comment counts ride the feed bubble, and publishes now additionally target the parent author's and tagged users' inbox relays, so a reply reaches authors who share no relay with us. The notifications pane gained an accurate tally strip with a 24h/7d/30d timeframe that remembers its choice.

The wallet got paste-time protection: relays inside wallet and bunker URIs are screened before any socket opens, private-address relays ask first, and consents are revocable in the settings pane. Cleartext ws:// relays are refused outright.

Media discipline: every pane pins exactly what is on screen, images stop disappearing while a page idles, RAM stops ballooning on photo profiles, and big pictures load now. Inline video plays its sound: the flatpak carries the PulseAudio permission. The pre-release five-lens audit fixed its verified findings: the pin registry is owner-keyed with a per-owner byte cap, closed panes release their pins, the consent ledger is written atomically with 0600 permissions, and preferences sync defers to newer local edits.

The replies-and-repairs release. Replies became surfaces, not a page: the composer sheet opens from any action row, thread included (the full form with attachments, alt text, preview and schedule in a card over the current pane), and the zap sheet became a proper overlay with its own card. Notifications wear their glyph anatomy: a reaction leads with its emoji, and reposts and quotes join the pane. Follow and Mute sit grouped on the profile, and the undo toast tells the truth past its deadline.

Signing got its biggest reliability pass yet: the first sign after login works against strict signers, the first sign after a restart carries the pairing secret the URI issued, and signing out and back in no longer strands the app on the login doors.

Under the hood: net_guard is the one IP authority, and the pre-release audit fixed ten verified findings: no more per-frame signature verification on zap rows, no resident tasks behind closed panes, the upload client and video player respect the IP authority, signer responses log method names only (the log file is 0600), and the single-instance socket read is capped.

An iteration release with no theme: the composer grew a Video tab (a deliberate video post is its own NIP-71 event, instant or scheduled, videos only), thread notes now carry the full action row the timeline has (reactions, repost, quote, reply, delete, zap), and the gallery carousel's arrows and position dots page the gallery instead of opening the thread.

Under the hood: paste-time screening refuses wallet and bunker URIs whose relays point at private addresses, the publish path refuses expired events and records its own deletions as tombstones at the door, and dependencies are current (cargo audit reports zero vulnerabilities). A CI workflow now gates every pull request, with a cargo-deny pass beside the audit.

New in the final cut: a store vacuum (satori-desktop --vacuum rebuilds the LMDB store offline, recovering the space deletions left behind) and an Alpine package beside the deb, rpm and flatpak - the first musl build.

The media and long-form release: attachments publish right (a note with an image is a kind-1 note with imeta; replies keep their thread), the Photo tab returns as its own picture-post surface, a full article composer (title, summary, cover upload, topics, markdown body) with strikethrough, task lists and tables in the reader, and hardenened media fetching (DNS-rebinding-safe resolution, search only asks search-capable relays).

The composer grew a polish pass of its own: previews on every tab (the article flips to the reader-faithful view, the rest show the draft as its feed card), session drafts for every post type with a two-step escape (the first escape saves and stays), a real editor (word motion, word deletion, line-wise home and end, a body that scrolls), fields that wrap and grow instead of clipping, video attachments in notes, a live reading time on the article, the type selector as a segmented control, and one filled action bar where Publish is unmistakable. A tag bug that kept satori's own polls from rendering as ballots is fixed.

The trust release: web of trust (in your network / outside, always annotated, never hidden), a duplicate-content spam filter with receipts, an auditable notification tier, and the four-lens audit fixes.

The polish release: live feed engagement, the relay hint model, scheduled posts, a full visual pass, and the quick wins (keyboard nav, emoji typeahead, multi-image carousel, alt text, relay health pane).
The first release: the whole client, from the follows timeline to inline video and zaps.
